title: Apollo spacesuits were sewn by a bra maker
hook: The suits worn on the Moon came from the company that made Playtex bras.
peek: Every astronaut who walked on the Moon wore a suit made by a division of the company behind Playtex bras and girdles. Its seamstresses stitched about 21 layers together, to tolerances finer than a millimetre.
lede: The suits worn by all twelve moonwalkers were not built by a big aerospace firm. They came from ILC, a division of the International Latex Corporation, the company that sold Playtex bras and girdles. Its workers already knew how to make soft, stretchy rubber garments that fit the body closely, and that turned out to be exactly the skill a flexible spacesuit needed.

bullets.text: ILC's Apollo suit, the A7L, had about 21 layers, from a rubber bladder holding in air to tough outer fabric that protected against heat and tiny space debris. It had to stay airtight while letting astronauts bend, kneel and pick up rocks.

The suits were sewn at ILC's factory in Dover, Delaware, largely by women who had made Playtex products. Seams had to be accurate to about a sixty-fourth of an inch, roughly 0.4 millimetres, with no room for error.

ILC was the underdog. It won the Apollo suit contract after tests in which its soft, flexible designs outperformed rival suits from larger defence contractors, whose stiffer designs were harder to move in.

The company, now called ILC Dover, kept making space gear. It built parts of the spacesuits used on the Space Shuttle and the International Space Station, and the airbags that cushioned the Mars Pathfinder landing in 1997.
